subject: Urgent: rapid evidence & log handling for May 21 latency spike
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@orendahealth.com>
To: ops+oncall@orendahealth.com; naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed 6-10x latency + 504s starting 09:05 PDT (prod)

Hi Naomi / Redwood oncall,

We started seeing a severe latency spike at ~09:05 PDT this morning affecting our payment flows. Error rate for token-generation calls jumped from ~0.2% to ~18% and end-to-end latency for critical route /v1/generate averaged 2.4s (baseline 220ms). We captured a sample of failing request IDs and attached a compressed log bundle (runtime_logs_20280521.tar.gz) via our ticketing system.

Immediate asks:
- Please preserve all runtime and agent logs for 04:45–10:15 PDT (UTC-7) — do not rotate or delete.
- Provide a short provenance note (what nodes handled these requests, model variant used, any automatic fallback events) suitable for our SOC/incident team.
- We will likely request an evidentiary export to attach to our internal review; confirm the secure transfer options (SFTP, signed Drive link, or Redbox secure share).

We are escalating to our execs (cc'd CFO) so we need a concise packet within 6 hours.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Director, SRE — OrendaHealth

---
Attachments: runtime_logs_20280521.tar.gz (log bundle, ~120MB)
From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Observed 6-10x latency + 504s starting 09:05 PDT (prod)

Julia — thanks for the rapid heads-up and the logs. We're treating this as high priority. Summary of immediate steps we are executing now: 

1) Preservation: enforce legal-hold on runtime logs and KV caches for the window 04:45–10:15 PDT; snapshot of request/response traces and model-serve metrics being stored to immutable bucket.
2) Triage: Marcus and team are collecting node-level metrics (GPU utilization, queue lengths, batching statistics) and looking for autoscaler/fallback triggers.
3) Evidence packaging: we can produce a forensic packet (logs + manifest + chain-of-custody) and deliver via a password-protected S3 presigned URL or enterprise SFTP; we will not share raw keys in email.

Questions for your SOC/Legal: any required redaction (PHI fields) before transfer? If so we will apply field-level redaction and provide a redaction manifest.

I'll assemble a 1–page executive brief and a technical packet. Expect the exec brief within 90 minutes and an initial forensic packet within 4–6 hours.

— Naomi

On Tue, May 21, 2028 at 09:28 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marcus and team are collecting node-level metrics...

Notes from initial triage (summary):
- Spike correlated with a sudden increase in short-sequence burst traffic on region-us-west2. Batching window grew from median 5ms -> 60ms which caused queueing and timeout cascades for sync routes.
- Two worker pools experienced kernel OOM on one airflow node; fallback policy triggered model-variant downgrade on several requests (quantized ~8-bit). We have the fallback event IDs.
- No indications of malicious injection; traffic patterns match legitimate customer load but concentrated on a few golden routes.

For the packet: I will produce
- node_manifest.txt (hostname, instance id, container id, model variant, kernel versions)
- request_id_index.csv (list of customer-provided request IDs with timestamps)
- batch_stats_{start,end}.json (batch size distribution)

I will attach a draft chain_of_custody_template.pdf to the packet and mark which files are hashed (SHA256).

Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
